bull_bear.body: CAR 18.85% (all Tier-1); enabling Rs 4,000 cr raise for growth (management comfort floor ~18%; consumes ~63 bps/qtr). Chose not to do Tier-2 (shallow market, poor rates). Large "hidden" regulatory capital (~Rs 9,000 cr delta: DTAs + Shriram/Pramerica investment book) to be released over time. M&A optional, not imminent.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **IT-sector salaried stress, South India** — early-bucket bounces up (13% of unsecured salaried base); *counter-intuitively visible in secured, not unsecured*; "breaking news," no flow to deeper buckets yet — underwriting already tightened on the margin.
- **LAP** — small Q1 uptick (4 idiosyncratic cases); "seat belts on," Q2 started well.
- **Small-ticket housing demand** organically weak industry-wide.
- **Wholesale prepayments** structurally cap wholesale AUM growth.
- West Asia conflict: no visible portfolio impact yet (possible lag).
- Capital raise timing/dilution.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Framework-disciplined (Growth/Profitability/Predictability), high-disclosure, self-critical. Jairam repeatedly hedged the IT-stress signal ("take it as breaking news … don't make too much of it") — flagged proactively rather than buried. Honest on NIM optics (DA pinch-hitter, calendar effect) and on PCR being an ECL output, not a target. Youngest upper-layer NBFC framing (retail phase ~5 yrs post-DHFL) used to argue a long profitability-expansion runway.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The RoAUM story is an **opex story**, not a yield story — 57 bps of the 33 bps RoAUM gain came from opex ratio; yields are flat by design.
- IT-salaried stress showing in *secured* before *unsecured* is the genuinely novel, non-consensus data point — inverts the usual stress-transmission and is worth tracking sector-wide.
- Wholesale "headwind" (61% of FY27 repayments already prepaid) is actually a portfolio-quality flex — RE cash flows beating underwriting.
- Capital raise is pre-emptive (enabling), not need-driven — 18.85% CAR is comfortable; the ~Rs 9,000 cr locked regulatory capital (DTA + Shriram book) is a future ROE unlock.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Balance sheet run at moderate leverage: net worth Rs 28,906 Cr, gross debt Rs 82,345 Cr, debt-to-equity 2.8x, and AUM-to-equity of 3.7x - the deck's AUM/E series rises from 2.1x in Q1 FY24 to 3.7x in Q1 FY27 against a long range goal marker.
- Capital adequacy of 18.85% at Jun-26, versus 19.77% at Mar-26 and 19.29% at Jun-25.
- Liquidity held deliberately high: cash and liquid investments of Rs 6,925 Cr (6% of assets) and Q1 FY27 consolidated LCR of 553% on a period-average basis against a 100% regulatory LCR requirement for NBFCs.
- Funding is being diversified "via MFs, ECB & securitisation"; borrowing by instrument type is Loans 42%, NCDs/Bonds 31%, ECB 19%, Securitization 7%, CP 1% and Public Issue 1%, with long-term domestic ratings of AA+/Stable from CRISIL, ICRA and CARE, international ratings of S&P BB and Moody's Ba3, and new Japanese agency ratings of R&I BBB/Stable and JCRA BBB/Stable.
- Non-lending stakes are retained and contribute associate income: investments in Shriram group of Rs 1,372 Cr and in alternatives and others of Rs 3,105 Cr, with associate income of Rs 82 Cr from Alternatives and Rs 17 Cr from Pramerica Life Insurance in Q1 FY27.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Mortgages Rs 61,199 cr (+30%)** = 57% of company / 67% of retail AUM; mass-affluent HL + larger-ticket "LAP Plus" growing fastest (AA+ upgrade enables serving these). Small-ticket affordable housing demand organically weak (industry low-single-digit/negative).
- **Unsecured Rs 21,412 cr (+45%)** across PL, UBL, digital/embedded, rural micro — 20% of company AUM. Risk at best levels in 2+ years; rural micro at all-time-best ratios. Digital (embedded/FLDG, 80%+) is high-beta on volume; Fintech activity picked up last 2 quarters.
- **Wholesale Rs 13,238 cr (+27%)**, RE:CMML 70:30, yield 14.2% (moderating on better rating mix). Elevated prepayments = real-estate cash flows running ahead of underwriting + CMML bank refinance/capital-market takeouts — a growth headwind but a quality signal.
- **Legacy Rs 2,452 cr** (2% of AUM), down Rs 355 cr.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Affordable-housing cost leadership:** operating at ~12.5% in <Rs 35 lakh housing — management frames Piramal itself as "the disruptor over the last 4-5 years" in that segment, not a victim of competition. AA+ rating structurally lowers cost of funds vs affordable-HFC peers.
- **Enterprise AI at genuine scale:** 320 bn AI tokens in Q1 (vs 178 bn Q4, 63 bn a year ago) at *flat* token cost (mix-shift to homegrown SLMs/open-source); credit-staff productivity +50% in 2 years. Launched "Pia," an AI investor-relations assistant (claimed first-of-kind external tool). Credible operating-efficiency moat (cost-to-income 72%→53% in 2 years).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Blueprint framed on three axes - Growth, Profitability, Predictability - to "Build a future-proof, AI-native company", against "long range goals as disclosed in August 2023" of "2x AUM in ~3 years", "RoAUM >3%" and "Stable Risk / Steady Earnings".
- AUM of Rs 1,06,940 Cr as of Jun-26 (up 25% YoY), of which retail AUM is Rs 91,249 Cr (up 32% YoY); retail:wholesale AUM mix has moved to 85:15 from 80:20 in Jun-25.
- Growth AUM (retail + wholesale, excluding the discontinued Legacy business) "are now 98% of total AUM" and are scaling at 32% YoY, versus 25% YoY for total AUM.
- Claims to be "one of the fastest among retail NBFCs to grow AUM from Rs 20k Cr to Rs 90k Cr" - Piramal Finance in ~4 yrs against peer NBFC A ~5 yrs, NBFC B ~8 yrs and NBFC C ~9 yrs (source stated as company data, 6 peers across diversified and vehicle financiers).
- Customer profile skews mass-market and non-metro: of customers acquired at urban branches in Q1 FY27, 82% are outside tier-1 markets, 56% are self-employed, the median customer earns Rs 49k monthly and is 38 years old; urban-branch customers represent 91% of total retail AUM.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Merger] The issuer is "Piramal Finance Limited (Formerly known as Piramal Capital & Housing Finance Limited)", and the deck cautions that "Historical information for Q1 FY26 and before is presented as previously disclosed and pertains to Piramal Enterprises before the merger with Piramal Finance in September 2025" - so pre-Sep-2025 series are not like-for-like with the current entity.
- [Legacy run-down] Legacy AUM is down to Rs 2,452 Cr, ~2% of total AUM, described as "AUM down 94% since March 2022" from Rs 43,175 Cr in FY22, with -61% YoY in Q1 FY27.
- [Divestments] Q4 FY26 exceptionals are footnoted as including gains of Rs 263 Cr from the Shriram LI stake sale and deferred consideration of Rs 1,326 Cr from the Piramal Imaging sale in 2018.
- [Investor relations] Launched "Pia (Piramal Investor Assistant)", an AI-powered investor relations agent hosted at piramalfinance.com/investors, positioned to answer financial line-item and past-earnings-call queries round-the-clock.
- [Filing context] The 10 August 2026 cover letter files this deck for the Motilal Oswal 22nd Annual Global Investor Conference on 17 August 2026, but the deck itself is the Q1 FY27 Results Presentation dated 16 July 2026 - i.e. re-used results material, not fresh conference content.

latest_quarter.body: NIM 6.5% (Growth 6.8%); the QoQ softness is DA-choice + calendar, not pricing. Cost of borrowing 8.80% (-4 bps QoQ) with AA+ tailwind ahead; minimal CP exposure cushioned dislocated Q1 wholesale funding markets. Opex +10% vs revenue +37% — the operating-leverage engine (opex/AUM down 3.5 yrs straight). Floating-rate mortgages: no PLR cut through the down-cycle, so lower rate-cut pass-through obligation on the way up ("lower amplitude both ways").
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** AUM Rs 1,06,940 cr (+25%; Growth +32%), consol PAT Rs 461 cr (+67%), RoAUM 1.9% (from 1.5%), cost-to-income 53%. **AA→AA+ upgrade** (+ Japanese R&I/JCR BBB/Stable). Retail 90+ 0.7% (no Q1 seasonal deterioration). Board OK'd enabling **Rs 4,000 cr** raise. New flag: **IT-salaried stress (South), visible in secured**. Launched "Pia" AI IR assistant; 320 bn AI tokens. Gold loans 67 branches (→200 by Mar-27).
- _Next Q → check: RoAUM path to 2.5% exit-Q4; IT-salaried stress — flow into deeper buckets / spread beyond South?; LAP 90+ (does the Q1 uptick persist?); capital raise executed?; gold-branch build toward 200; PL branch penetration to ~100%; AA+ cost-of-borrowing benefit showing up; wholesale AUM vs prepayment drag._

outlook.body:

- Claims to be "one of the fastest among retail NBFCs to grow AUM from Rs 20k Cr to Rs 90k Cr" - Piramal Finance in ~4 yrs against peer NBFC A ~5 yrs, NBFC B ~8 yrs and NBFC C ~9 yrs (source stated as company data, 6 peers across diversified and vehicle financiers).
- Customer profile skews mass-market and non-metro: of customers acquired at urban branches in Q1 FY27, 82% are outside tier-1 markets, 56% are self-employed, the median customer earns Rs 49k monthly and is 38 years old; urban-branch customers represent 91% of total retail AUM.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Mortgages Rs 61,199 cr (+30%)** = 57% of company / 67% of retail AUM; mass-affluent HL + larger-ticket "LAP Plus" growing fastest (AA+ upgrade enables serving these). Small-ticket affordable housing demand organically weak (industry low-single-digit/negative).
- **Unsecured Rs 21,412 cr (+45%)** across PL, UBL, digital/embedded, rural micro — 20% of company AUM. Risk at best levels in 2+ years; rural micro at all-time-best ratios. Digital (embedded/FLDG, 80%+) is high-beta on volume; Fintech activity picked up last 2 quarters.
- **Wholesale Rs 13,238 cr (+27%)**, RE:CMML 70:30, yield 14.2% (moderating on better rating mix). Elevated prepayments = real-estate cash flows running ahead of underwriting + CMML bank refinance/capital-market takeouts — a growth headwind but a quality signal.
- **Legacy Rs 2,452 cr** (2% of AUM), down Rs 355 cr.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline — N/A (financial)
order_book.body: Disbursements +44% YoY. Retail franchise 6 mn customers (+24%); cross-sell = 28% of unsecured disbursement (target materially higher). Branches 780 (net +79): gold 67, rural 178, urban 535 (closed 8 full-service urban). Wholesale disbursed Rs 2,604 cr across 73 transactions (38 new); repayments Rs 1,932 cr (74% of disbursed) — ~61% of FY27 contractual wholesale repayments already prepaid.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 guidance reaffirmed** (AUM growth, profit growth, RoAUM) — "confident of meeting original guidance provided last quarter"; Growth AUM sustaining in the 30s%.
- **RoAUM:** 1.8-1.9% (Q1) → **2.5% by exit Q4 FY27**; lever = larger year-end book on flat people cost (staff increments front-loaded in Q1).
- **Opex/AUM:** retail at 3.5%, to move further lower through FY27; ~40-50 bps more value over next 4-5 quarters.
- **Gold loans:** 67 branches (Q1) → **200 branches by end-March 2027** (phase-2 launched).
- **PL branch penetration:** to ~100% "over next 2-3 quarters."
- **Leverage:** 4.5-5x long-range goal (set when AA-rated; likely revised higher as AA+ beds in).
- **Capital:** board-approved enabling raise up to Rs 4,000 cr, "at an appropriate time post shareholder approval" (growth capital; CAR comfort floor ~18% vs 15% regulatory).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Gold loans (67→200 branches by Mar-27) + rural micro (branch build-out); cross-sell scale-up (lower opex/credit cost); larger-ticket secured mortgages post-AA+; embedded/digital finance (capital-light, FLDG). Possible inorganic M&A ("Piramal house has used M&A for value creation"; open but nothing imminent, unrelated to the raise).

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: NIM 6.5% (Growth 6.8%); the QoQ softness is DA-choice + calendar, not pricing. Cost of borrowing 8.80% (-4 bps QoQ) with AA+ tailwind ahead; minimal CP exposure cushioned dislocated Q1 wholesale funding markets. Opex +10% vs revenue +37% — the operating-leverage engine (opex/AUM down 3.5 yrs straight). Floating-rate mortgages: no PLR cut through the down-cycle, so lower rate-cut pass-through obligation on the way up ("lower amplitude both ways").

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: CAR 18.85% (all Tier-1); enabling Rs 4,000 cr raise for growth (management comfort floor ~18%; consumes ~63 bps/qtr). Chose not to do Tier-2 (shallow market, poor rates). Large "hidden" regulatory capital (~Rs 9,000 cr delta: DTAs + Shriram/Pramerica investment book) to be released over time. M&A optional, not imminent.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Framework-disciplined (Growth/Profitability/Predictability), high-disclosure, self-critical. Jairam repeatedly hedged the IT-stress signal ("take it as breaking news … don't make too much of it") — flagged proactively rather than buried. Honest on NIM optics (DA pinch-hitter, calendar effect) and on PCR being an ECL output, not a target. Youngest upper-layer NBFC framing (retail phase ~5 yrs post-DHFL) used to argue a long profitability-expansion runway.

moat.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position (OPTIONAL)
moat.body:
- **Affordable-housing cost leadership:** operating at ~12.5% in <Rs 35 lakh housing — management frames Piramal itself as "the disruptor over the last 4-5 years" in that segment, not a victim of competition. AA+ rating structurally lowers cost of funds vs affordable-HFC peers.
- **Enterprise AI at genuine scale:** 320 bn AI tokens in Q1 (vs 178 bn Q4, 63 bn a year ago) at *flat* token cost (mix-shift to homegrown SLMs/open-source); credit-staff productivity +50% in 2 years. Launched "Pia," an AI investor-relations assistant (claimed first-of-kind external tool). Credible operating-efficiency moat (cost-to-income 72%→53% in 2 years).

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **IT-sector salaried stress, South India** — early-bucket bounces up (13% of unsecured salaried base); *counter-intuitively visible in secured, not unsecured*; "breaking news," no flow to deeper buckets yet — underwriting already tightened on the margin.
- **LAP** — small Q1 uptick (4 idiosyncratic cases); "seat belts on," Q2 started well.
- **Small-ticket housing demand** organically weak industry-wide.
- **Wholesale prepayments** structurally cap wholesale AUM growth.
- West Asia conflict: no visible portfolio impact yet (possible lag).
- Capital raise timing/dilution.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The RoAUM story is an **opex story**, not a yield story — 57 bps of the 33 bps RoAUM gain came from opex ratio; yields are flat by design.
- IT-salaried stress showing in *secured* before *unsecured* is the genuinely novel, non-consensus data point — inverts the usual stress-transmission and is worth tracking sector-wide.
- Wholesale "headwind" (61% of FY27 repayments already prepaid) is actually a portfolio-quality flex — RE cash flows beating underwriting.
- Capital raise is pre-emptive (enabling), not need-driven — 18.85% CAR is comfortable; the ~Rs 9,000 cr locked regulatory capital (DTA + Shriram book) is a future ROE unlock.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Merger] The issuer is "Piramal Finance Limited (Formerly known as Piramal Capital & Housing Finance Limited)", and the deck cautions that "Historical information for Q1 FY26 and before is presented as previously disclosed and pertains to Piramal Enterprises before the merger with Piramal Finance in September 2025" - so pre-Sep-2025 series are not like-for-like with the current entity.
- [Legacy run-down] Legacy AUM is down to Rs 2,452 Cr, ~2% of total AUM, described as "AUM down 94% since March 2022" from Rs 43,175 Cr in FY22, with -61% YoY in Q1 FY27.
- [Divestments] Q4 FY26 exceptionals are footnoted as including gains of Rs 263 Cr from the Shriram LI stake sale and deferred consideration of Rs 1,326 Cr from the Piramal Imaging sale in 2018.
- [Investor relations] Launched "Pia (Piramal Investor Assistant)", an AI-powered investor relations agent hosted at piramalfinance.com/investors, positioned to answer financial line-item and past-earnings-call queries round-the-clock.
- [Filing context] The 10 August 2026 cover letter files this deck for the Motilal Oswal 22nd Annual Global Investor Conference on 17 August 2026, but the deck itself is the Q1 FY27 Results Presentation dated 16 July 2026 - i.e. re-used results material, not fresh conference content.
